description:
1997 American Platinum Eagle containing 1/4 troy ounce of .9995 fine platinum, from the inaugural year of the U.S. Mint’s Platinum Eagle program. The obverse features John Mercanti’s Statue of Liberty portrait; the reverse features Thomas D. Rogers’ eagle soaring above a rising sun, with the platinum purity, weight and $25 denomination. Bullion issue with no mint, housed in a clear protective flip with the dealer’s labels.
Offered from the inventory of a recently retired Wisconsin numismatic dealer whose esteemed career spanned nearly five decades. Widely known and respected by fellow dealers and collectors across the country, he was a familiar, trusted presence at coin and antique shows. He provided coin collection appraisals for banks, jewelry stores, insurance companies, and private clients. He also served as president of civic and professional numismatic organizations, and played an integral role in the early lobbying efforts toward Wisconsin’s eventual sales tax exemption for precious metal bullion sales.
***This is a SHIPPING ONLY auction! All items will be fully insured. Items will be shipped on Monday October 26. By placing your bid, you agree to pay the shipping and handling fees. There is NO in person pickup option for this auction!

: Bring a touch of industrial history to your space with this collection of 10 assorted color Hemingray glass insulators. Each piece offers its unique patina, displaying hues of clear, aqua, and light green glass with vintage charm and visible air bubbles, mold seams, and embossed markings. These insulators, once used on telegraph and telephone poles, now offer collectors and decorators a glimpse into classic American utility design. Whether grouped together or displayed individually, their rounded shapes and subtle imperfections enhance their visual appeal. The glass construction ensures long-lasting durability, while the recognizable Hemingray embossing adds legitimacy and collector value. Ideal for display in a curio cabinet, as paperweights, or for upcycling in home decor projects, this lot brings both style and history. All items are in used condition with some signs of age, minor dirt, and expected wear, but no obvious major cracks or chips. Perfect for collectors or those seeking distinctive vintage decor

description:
Glass Insulator Lot - 3 Pieces
Hemingray and American Manufactured
Aqua Teal and Clear, Vintage Mid-Century Era
This collection of three vintage glass insulators represents a significant era in American telecommunications history. Used primarily to insulate telegraph and telephone wires from their wooden support poles, these heavy glass pieces are prized by collectors for their industrial aesthetic and vibrant glass colors. This lot provides a balanced display including a classic aqua teal piece and two clear glass specimens.
Pieces Included:
Hemingray Insulator, Aqua Teal Glass, embossed "HEMINGRAY" with beaded drip points - minor base fleabites
Clear Glass Insulator, embossed "MADE IN U.S.A.", smooth base - excellent vintage condition
Unmarked Clear Glass Insulator, smooth base - excellent vintage condition
Condition:
The lot is in very good vintage condition. The teal Hemingray insulator shows typical minor chipping and roughness along the drip points on the base, which is characteristic of utility-grade glass. The clear insulators are notably well-preserved with no significant chips or cracks. All pieces retain their original glossy transparency without signs of glass disease or mineral cloudiness.

Lionel Postwar O Gauge Flatcar Lot - 2 Pieces With Original Boxes
No. 6801 Flatcar with Boat & No. 6477 Bulkhead Flatcar with Pipe Load
Postwar Era, Made in USA
This vintage lot features two classic Postwar Lionel O gauge freight cars accompanied by their original boxes. Included are the No. 6801 flatcar equipped with its white cradle and blue-and-white plastic cabin cruiser boat, along with the No. 6477 bulkhead flatcar carrying a structural pipe load secured between side stakes. Produced during the late 1950s, these workhorse freight cars showcase the ingenuity and charm of Lionel's golden era of model railroading.
Lionel No. 6801 red flatcar with white cradle and blue/white runabout boat marked 6801-50
Lionel No. 6477 red bulkhead flatcar with black end racks, vertical side stakes, and pipe load
Both cars feature operational knuckle couplers and die-cast metal trucks
Includes two original Lionel Corporation classic orange-and-blue illustrated boxes
Condition:
Flatcars display light play wear consistent with age, including faint surface scuffs and light oxidation on metal axles and couplers. The boat shows mild dust accumulation and age-related toning to the cream plastic deck. Pipe load exhibits minor surface marks. Both boxes have shelf wear, edge creasing, and flap wear, with one box missing end flaps. Complete as pictured.
Warehouse Location: Cleveland

Natural Mineral Collection
Assorted Crystal Geodes and Quartz Clusters
Natural Stone / Mineral Specimens

This diverse collection features a variety of natural mineral specimens, highlighting the geometric beauty of crystalline formations. The lot includes a prominent deep purple amethyst cluster with well-defined terminations, alongside numerous white quartz druzy geodes and clusters. Several specimens exhibit a reddish-orange iron staining, providing a warm contrast to the translucent and opaque white quartz structures. The collection offers a range of geological textures, from hollow geode cavities to solid crystalline matrices.

description:
Glass Insulator Lot - 3 Pieces
Hemingray, Ohio Valley Glass Co. (O.V.G. Co.)
Aqua and Teal Green, Vintage
Collection of three vintage glass insulators originally utilized for telegraph and telephone line insulation. This lot features insulators from prominent American manufacturers, showcasing the industrial aqua and teal green glass common to early 20th-century utility production. These heavy pressed glass pieces are sought after for their historical industrial aesthetic and display appeal.
Pieces Included:
Insulator, Aqua, marked "O.V.G. CO." - features a large chip on the side and base
Insulator, Teal Green, marked "N 21" - internal vertical crack visible on the crown
Insulator, Aqua/Teal, marked "HEMINGRAY" - exhibits surface scratching and minor flea bites
Condition:
The lot is in damaged vintage condition as noted and photographed. One insulator has a significant chip loss on the lower body. A second piece shows a distinct crack through the glass dome. The Hemingray piece retains its shape but shows signs of outdoor weathering and light surface wear. Recommended for rustic decor or craft projects.

Selenite Gypsum Crystal Slab on Matrix Rock
Rough Geological Specimen, Approximately 6.5 x 5 x 1.5 Inches
This natural geological specimen consists of a substantial plate of translucent crystalline selenite (gypsum) anchored to a sandy sedimentary rock matrix. Selenite crystal plates of this type form through evaporation in saline basins and exhibit distinct basal cleavage, glassy to pearly surface luster, and natural surface texturing. Specimens retaining their natural host rock provide valuable educational and aesthetic display value for mineral collectors.

description:
Artist Unknown
Mixed Gemstone Wall Cross
Mixed Rocks and Gemstones on Wood Support
12" x 9" x 1.5"
Unsigned
This elaborate handmade wall cross features a dense mosaic of raw and tumbled gemstones. The piece is constructed on a solid wooden base with a white textured aggregate ground. The composition includes a diverse array of natural specimens, including amethyst, rose quartz, and jasper, showcasing a wide spectrum of natural colors and textures typical of contemporary folk art.
Features a multifaceted array of natural mineral specimens in raw and polished states
Sturdy wooden construction with integrated metal screw-eye for wall mounting
Textured white base coat enhances the visual pop of the colorful gemstones
Condition:
Very good handmade condition with stones securely attached. Wood backing is sound with minor surface wear consistent with the crafting process. Natural irregularities in the stones are inherent to the design.

title: Hemingray 42 Glass Insulator Set 2 Aqua Blue Green CD 154 Made in USA Vintage
description:
Hemingray Glass Company Set - 2 Pieces
Hemingray 42 (CD 154)
Aqua, Vintage Mid-Century
This set features two vintage aqua glass insulators produced by the Hemingray Glass Company, identified by the "Hemingray-42" mold mark. The No. 42 model, classified as CD 154 by collectors, was one of the most widely used designs for telephone and telegraph lines across North America during the early-to-mid 20th century. Prized for their deep aqua color and iconic industrial aesthetic, these pieces represent a significant era of American telecommunications history and are staple items for glass insulator collectors.
Pieces Included:
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Glass Insulator, Hemingray 42, Aqua, Beaded Base - minor fleabites on drip points
Condition:
Both insulators are in good vintage condition with characteristic wear expected from outdoor utility use. The glass retains high clarity and its original vibrant aqua hue. As is common with authentic vintage insulators, there are minor fleabites and small chips along the sharp drip points on the beaded base. No large structural cracks or major damage to the wire grooves or top domes observed.

When an order includes both flat-rate and dimensional-weight items, shipping may be calculated using dimensional weight. Combining these items does not necessarily reduce shipping costs and may result in the same or higher shipping charges than purchasing them separately.
